#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#
# New property defined: If a node holds the lock, then its epoch is the highest.
# Modification: Got rid of first non-zero epoch (since not necessary).

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] held(N1) -> le(ep(N2), ep(N1))

invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant transfer(E, N) -> ~held(N)

invariant held(N) -> ~transfer(E, N)

invariant locked(E, N) -> ~held(N)

invariant held(N) -> ~locked(E, N)

invariant transfer(E, N) -> le(ep(N), E)

invariant locked(E, N) -> le(ep(N), E)

invariant transfer(E1, N) & transfer(E2, N) -> E1 = E2

invariant locked(E1, N) & locked(E2, N) -> E1 = E2

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#
# New property defined: If a node holds the lock, then its epoch is the highest.
# Modification: Got rid of first non-zero epoch (since not necessary).

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] held(N1) -> le(ep(N2), ep(N1))

invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant transfer(E, N) -> ~held(N)

invariant held(N) -> ~transfer(E, N)

invariant locked(E, N) -> ~held(N)

invariant held(N) -> ~locked(E, N)

invariant transfer(E, N) -> le(ep(N), E)

invariant locked(E, N) -> le(ep(N), E)

invariant transfer(E1, N) & transfer(E2, N) -> E1 = E2

invariant locked(E1, N) & locked(E2, N) -> E1 = E2

invariant held(N) -> forall E. ~transfer(E, N)

invariant transfer(E, N) -> ~le(E, ep(N))

invariant held(N1) -> forall E. ~locked(E, N1)

invariant transfer(E, N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant held(N) -> forall E. ~le(E, ep(N)) | ~transfer(E, N)

invariant transfer(E, N) & held(N2) & N ~= N2 -> le(ep(N2), E)

# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#
# New property defined: If a node holds the lock, then its epoch is the highest.
# Modification: Got rid of first non-zero epoch (since not necessary).

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant transfer(E, N) -> ~held(N)

invariant held(N) -> ~transfer(E, N)

invariant locked(E, N) -> ~held(N)

invariant held(N) -> forall E. ~transfer(E, N)

invariant held(N1) -> forall E. ~locked(E, N1)

invariant transfer(E, N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant held(N) -> forall E. ~le(E, ep(N)) | ~transfer(E, N)

invariant transfer(E, N) & held(N2) & N ~= N2 -> le(ep(N2), E)

invariant held(N) -> forall E. le(ep(N), E) | ~transfer(E, N)

- `a(x)` is true (x is active)
- `~reach(x)` is true (x cannot reach org)
- The preconditions about reachability are satisfied

The issue is that the preconditions of `test` are not sufficient to guarantee that `reach(x)` should be true. The action requires certain implications to hold, but these are just assumptions—they don't prevent the action from being called in a state where `reach(x)` is false.

The safety property `~error(N)` can only be maintained if we prevent `test` from ever setting `error(x) := true`. This means we need invariants that ensure whenever `test` is called with some `x`, the preconditions actually force `reach(x)` to be true, making the `require ~reach(x)` fail.

Looking at the preconditions of `test`:
1. `(s1(X, Y) & a(Y) & reach(Y)) -> reach(X)` — if first successor is active and reachable, then X is reachable
2. `(s1(X, Y) & ~a(Y) & s2(X, Z) & a(Z) & reach(Z)) -> reach(X)` — if first successor is inactive but second successor is active and reachable, then X is reachable
3. `(ring.btw(x, Y, org) & a(Y)) -> reach(Y)` — all active nodes between x and org are reachable
4. `a(x)` — x is active
5. `~reach(x)` — x is not reachable
6. `in_s1(x) -> exists Y. s1(x, Y)` — if in_s1 flag is set, there exists a successor
7. `in_s2(x) -> exists Y. s2(x, Y)` — if in_s2 flag is set, there exists a second successor

The key insight: if `in_s1(x)` is true, then there must exist a `Y` with `s1(x, Y)`. Combined with the first precondition, if that successor is active and reachable, then `x` must be reachable. So we need invariants ensuring that:
- If `in_s1(x)` is true and `s1(x, Y)` holds, then either `a(Y)` is false or `reach(Y)` is false (to avoid forcing `reach(x)` true)
- Or more directly: `reach(x)` must be true whenever the conditions would force it

The simplest approach: add invariants that ensure `reach(org)` is always true, and that reachability propagates correctly through the successor pointers.

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node
individual firste:epoch
axiom firste ~= zero

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := firste if N = first else zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
#    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant held(N) -> ~transfer(ep(N), N)
invariant ~(held(N1) & held(N2)) | N1 = N2
invariant transfer(E, N1) & transfer(E, N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant locked(E, N) -> ~transfer(E, N)
invariant held(N) & locked(E, N) -> ep(N) = E

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {

    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality

################################################################################

# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

1. **Pre-state**: `msg_2b(0,1,0) = true` (acceptor 0 voted for value 0 in ballot 1)
2. **Action**: `phase_2b(a=0, b=0, v=1)` is called
3. **Post-state**: `msg_2b(0,0,1) = true` (acceptor 0 now voted for value 1 in ballot 0)

This violates the safety property because:
- `chosenAt(1,0)` is true (value 0 chosen in ballot 1)
- `chosenAt(0,1)` becomes true (value 1 chosen in ballot 0)
- Both `chosen(0)` and `chosen(1)` are true, violating safety

The root cause: **an acceptor voted for different values in different ballots**. The `phase_2b` action allows acceptor 0 to vote for value 1 in ballot 0, even though it already voted for value 0 in ballot 1.

The key invariant needed: **once an acceptor votes for a value in a ballot, it cannot vote for a different value in any ballot**. More precisely, if an acceptor has voted in ballot B for value V, then in any other ballot it can only vote for V (or not vote at all).

Additionally, we need to ensure that `maxBal` is consistent with actual votes, and that the protocol respects the constraint that an acceptor's `maxBal` should reflect its actual voting history.
